notes: The chart title is ellipsised to "Favori..." in both modes even though the card has plenty of unused width; the title should wrap or the chart should use the full card width.

Wrong-answer explanation reads "1 icons x 10 = 10." (singular/plural bug) and never says to look at the Apple row; the prompt "How many apples are there?" also reads oddly against a "Favourite fruit" survey graph.

Long text choices have no horizontal padding: every option's first character sits on top of the pill's rounded border (left) and the text runs to the right border, and the 3-line option reaches the very bottom of the screen.
Chart title ellipsised to "Daily hi..." in both modes despite unused card width; "between 70 and 75" is also ambiguous about which bin a value of exactly 75 falls into.
Wrong-answer explanation is only "IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 9 - 6 = 3" - it never says Q1 and Q3 are the left and right edges of the box, so a kid who missed it cannot see where 6 and 9 came from.
Explanation says "Sum: 95" without listing the addends (17 + 17 + 19 + 20 + 22), so a kid who added wrong cannot find their mistake.

Dot-plot axis labels every integer from 0 to 29 and they collide into an unreadable smear ("9 101 11 21 31 41 51 61 71 81 92 02 1..."), so the data values cannot be read in either mode; the dots at 15 and 16 also overlap. lib/presentation/diagrams/dot_plot.dart shrinks tick spacing to fit but never thins the labels.

Same dot-plot axis-label collision: the 2-38 axis prints a label at every integer and everything past ~10 is an illegible smear, so the highest and lowest values the question asks for cannot be read in either mode.

Worst case of the dot-plot axis-label collision: the 0-47 axis labels every integer and the whole strip is unreadable, so none of the seven data values can be identified from the diagram in either mode.
